question: Is there a growth law under which parts of the live roster that have come apart become one part again, so that what one part builds depends on whether another part is there: under the record's laws in which a birth takes a distinction that is already shared (rule Q, rule R as a treatment of a short knot, and the A225 move as a control placed by hand), and under a ladder of laws that take from a knot the parent meets or from an ancestor; at what cost; and how much of any positive is the scaffolds'?
inputs: The starts, base laws, taking rules, choices, swaps and bounds named in the pre-registration; this epic's definitions and the shared definitions of RING-IN-BALANCE-20261123-001; the ring study's engine and the other thread's rule-R and rule-Q engines, unchanged, for the gate.
forbidden_inputs: Any definition changed after a value is seen; for the engine's author, the drafter's scratch prototype and anything it produced beyond what the pre-registration discloses; any change to the engines used for the gate.
primary_observable: For every registered run: parts, classes, pairs that came apart, and for every registered pair the four marks (one part again, a joint birth, the course differs, the course differs with what the other is), the demand line, the way of each difference, the masked runs, the verdict (through a knot the growth made, through a start knot, supplied, unconfirmed) and the class of the linking knots; the cost of each law; the swaps each case survives; the knot test of every knot under the run's own knot law.
comparators_or_controls: The base laws with no taking rule; RECORD-k and ALL-JOINABLE; one control of the nearest-ancestor kind whose rule looks for the other part; the A225 birth placed by hand; the second part barred, and removed where that is defined; masked runs; the swaps of run 5.
resource_budget: Each run under ten minutes and 8 GB on one process; anything longer through the shared runner with a row in the long-running index. Bounds: 8 rounds; a run stops after the first round that leaves more than 1,500 knots; the guard of the pre-registration.
first_executable_signal: The gate P0; then whether any two parts that are wholly apart are ever one part again under rule Q or SHORT-TAKES (P1).
decision_rule: Each prediction is judged by its 'Fails when' column; checks and open items are reported as such.
stop_rule: Stop when each of rule Q, rule R and the A225 move has a verdict, and every law of the ladder that has the mark 'the course differs' through a meeting and is minimal in the cost order is identified with its cost, its verdict and the swaps it survives, or every registered law has failed with its reason; every registered run done and every prediction with a verdict.
nonclaims: An exploratory study of rules added by hand on starts built by hand, to eight rounds. A positive would show that a supplied rule can put two separated parts in one part again and that the first then builds differently; it would not show a reference (one bit crosses, by crowding), nor that the dependence carries what the other part is, nor anything about the model's own laws. The owner's conviction that such a law must exist (assumption A241) is recorded as his intuition and is not evidence. No claim about living things or minds.
